Rashi on Chullin 10b:10:1.hebrew: ועוד אחורי הדלת - אם היה נגע אחורי הדלת ביציאתו, היכי חזי ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:10:1.english: And furthermore, behind the door - If there was a nega [plague-mark] behind the door as he was going out, how could he see it?

Rashi on Chullin 10b:10:2.english: That had a small window opened into it - A window in the door, before the quarantine [was imposed].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:10:3.hebrew: אין פותחין - בית אפל שצריך לפתוח לו חלונות לראות הנגע, פוטרין אותו לגמרי, כדכתיב (ויקרא יד) כנגע נראה לי בבית, לי ולא לאורי, שאם עמד במקום אפל וצריך שם להדליק את הנר אינו נגע:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:10:3.english: We do not open - A dark house that would require opening windows for it in order to see the plague-mark is exempted entirely, as it is written (Leviticus 14): "Something like a plague has appeared to me in the house" - "to me," and not "to my light" - meaning that if he stood in a dark spot and would need to light a candle there [to see it], it is not deemed a plague.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:11:1.english: The High Priest on Yom Kippur - When he exits the Holy of Holies after taking out the spoon and the fire-pan, it is written, "and he shall go out and offer his burnt-offering," etc., in [the portion of] Acharei Mot.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:11:2.english: And we learned - In tractate Yoma (page 52b).

Rashi on Chullin 10b:11:3.english: He went out and came back the way he had entered - His face was toward the innermost sanctuary, just as when he entered; so too he turns around and goes out walking backwards.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:11:4.hebrew: דלא אתחזק - כל זמן שלא ראה הכהן את הנגע במראותיו, שהיה מקום אפל ואין מראהו ניכר. אבל נגע שעומד אחורי הדלת וכבר הכיר שהוא נגע, ואין צריך חלון אלא להעמידו בחזקתו - פותחין:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:11:4.english: That it was not established - As long as the priest has not [yet] seen the leprous mark in its [proper] light, because it was a dark place and its appearance could not be discerned. But a mark that is behind the door, and he has already recognized it as a mark, and he does not need a window except to maintain it in its established status - they do open [a window for it].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:12:1.hebrew: תניא דלא כרב אחא בר יעקב - דאמר דלא מוקי אחזקתו אלא ביצא דרך אחוריו, דחזי ליה עד שעת הסגר, דהכא קתני שאם הלך לביתו והסגירו, הסגרו הסגר, והכא ודאי איכסי נגע מיניה, ומוקמי ליה אחזקיה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:12:1.english: A baraita was taught not in accordance with Rav Acha bar Yaakov - who said that we rely on his presumptive status only if he went out walking backwards, so that the priest could keep him in view until the time of quarantine. For here it teaches that if he went to his house and was quarantined there, his quarantine is valid - and here the affliction was certainly hidden from the priest's view, yet we still rely on his presumptive status.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:12:2.english: One might think - that he has permission to go into his own house, and then come back and close the door.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:13:1.english: Under the lintel [ha-mashkof] - The upper threshold [of the doorway].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:14:1.english: (He went to his house and closed himself in - By means of a long rope, such as when his house was close to that place.)

Rashi on Chullin 10b:14:2.english: Inside the house - Under the lintel.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:15:1.hebrew: ורב אחא - אמר לך מהא לא תותבן, דאיכא לאוקמי:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:15:1.english: And Rav Acha - [Rav Acha bar Yaakov] could say to you: You cannot refute me from this [baraita], since it can be reconciled [with my opinion].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:1:1.english: And why is it different - This is a doubt and that is a doubt.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:2:1.english: The halakha is like Rav Huna - For we are concerned about the hide. And a case came before me, and my teacher Rabbeinu Yaakov the son of Rabbi Yakar ruled for me, concerning a bird, that it is forbidden.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:2:2.hebrew: מכלל דרב חסדא אפילו כשלא שיבר בה עצם - לאחר שחיטה מכשיר, מדאצטריך למימר הלכתא כרב הונא כשלא שיבר, מכלל דפליג רב חסדא עליה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:2:2.english: By inference, [the halakha follows] Rav Ḥisda even when he did not break a bone in it - [Rav Ḥisda] deems it valid [by attributing the notch to having occurred] after the slaughtering. Since it was necessary to state, "The halakha is in accordance with Rav Huna when he did not break a bone," this implies that Rav Ḥisda disagrees with him [in that case].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:2:3.hebrew: בעצם מפרקת - לאחר שחיטה שנגע בעצם הצואר, והיא המפרקת, דכתיב (שמואל א ד) ותשבר מפרקתו, ולא סבירא לן כוותיה למתלי לקולא, דההיא נגיעה דעצם מפרקת לא פגמה לסכין טפי מעור, אבל שבירת עצמות בההוא ודאי תלינן:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:2:3.english: On the neck-bone - [This refers to a case] after the slaughtering, where [the knife] touched the bone of the neck, which is the "mafreket," as it is written (I Samuel 4): "and his neck was broken" (va-tishaver mafrakto). But we do not hold like this, to rely leniently [on this to explain a nick found in the knife] - for that contact with the mafreket bone would not damage the knife any more than [contact with] skin would. But when it comes to an actual breaking of bones, in that case we certainly do attribute [the nick] to it.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:1.hebrew: תליסר חיותא - שלא בדק בין זו לזו, ולאחר שחיטת כולן נמצאת פגומה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:1.english: Thirteen animals - [Meaning,] he did not check [the knife] between one [slaughter] and the next, and after slaughtering all of them, it [the knife] was found to be flawed.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:2.english: According to whom - [Meaning:] According to whose opinion does he hold?

Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:3.hebrew: כרב הונא ואפילו בהמה קמייתא - נמי טרפה, דחיישינן לעור ולשון, בעיא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:3.english: In accordance with Rav Huna, and even the first animal - is also a tereifah, because we suspect [the notch resulted from contact with] the hide or the tongue; this is posed as an unresolved query.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:4.hebrew: לא כרב חסדא - ומשום עצם מפרקת דקמייתא, טרפינהו לכולהו בתרייתא:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:3:4.english: Not in accordance with Rav Chisda - Rather, it was because [the notch in the knife was known to have been caused] by the neck-bone of the first [animal], that he deemed all the subsequent ones tref.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:4:1.hebrew: מכדי מיתלא תלינן - דהא ודאי נגיעת סכין במפרקת לא פגמה טפי מעור, שהרי אינו מכה עליו בכח, ואפילו הכי תלי ביה לקולא, הלכך כי שחט בהמות טובא תלי נמי רב חסדא במפרקת דבתרייתא ומכשר להו:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:4:1.english: After all, we do rely [on the possibility] - For certainly the knife's touching the vertebrae did not nick it any more than [it nicked] the skin, since he does not strike it forcefully, and even so [Rav Chisda] relies on this to be lenient. Therefore, when he slaughtered many animals, Rav Chisda likewise relied on the vertebrae of the last [animal] and validated them.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:5:1.english: To invalidate the first one - This is [itself] an unresolved matter. The reason [the Gemara] requires checking [the knife] immediately after the first slaughter is that if he finds it nicked, he renders that [first animal] non-kosher, following Rav Huna['s opinion].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:5:2.hebrew: לא כרב חסדא - ס"ל דלא חייש לעור, ומצריך בדיקה, שאם תמצא פגומה יתקננה, ויהיו אחרונות כשרות עם הראשונה, דאי לא בדק ושחיט ליה לאידך, ומשכח לה פגומה, חיישינן למפרקת דקמייתא, ואסירי בתרייתא, ולית ליה הא דאמרן לעיל מכדי מתלא תלינן כו'. ואע"ג דמשנינא הכי, דיחויא בעלמא הוא, כלומר: לעולם אימא לך כרב חסדא סבירא ליה, אבל רב כהנא ודאי כרב הונא קאמר למפסל קמייתא, כדאוקמינן לעיל, הלכתא כוותיה. והשוחט אפילו בהמה אחת צריך לבדוק הסכין אחר שחיטה, ואם שחט הרבה ולא בדק בינתים, ואחר כך נמצאת פגומה, אף הראשונה אסורה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:5:2.english: Not like Rav Chisda - He [Rav Kahana] holds that one need not worry about [checking the knife because of] the hide, but requires checking [it after slaughtering]; so that if it is found flawed, he repairs it, and the later [animals slaughtered with it] are valid along with the first one. For if he did not check, and slaughtered another [animal] with it, and [then] finds it flawed, we suspect [the nick came from] the neck-joint of the first [animal], and [so] the later ones are forbidden - and he does not hold like what we said above, "Now, do we rely on the presumption... etc." And although we answered it this way [earlier], that is merely a deflection; that is to say: I could still tell you that he [Rav Kahana] does hold like Rav Chisda, but Rav Kahana certainly meant to say like Rav Huna, invalidating the first [animal], as we established above, and the halachah follows him. And one who slaughters even a single animal must check the knife after slaughtering; and if he slaughtered many [animals] without checking in between, and it was afterward found flawed, even the first [animal] is forbidden.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:6:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דמשום הא דבעי למישחטיה קא בדיק, הוי ליה בדיקה דקודם שחיטה, ותיבעי חכם להראות לו את הסכין, דילפינן (לקמן חולין יז:) מ"ושחטתם בזה ואכלתם", ומדלא בעי למחוי לחכם, ש"מ לאו בדיקה דקודם שחיטה חשיב ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:6:1.english: If so - [The Gemara asks:] Since he checks [the knife] precisely because he is about to slaughter with it, this checking would be one that occurs before the slaughter, and it should then require a sage, to whom he must show the knife, as we derive (below, Chullin 17b) from [the verse] "you shall slaughter it in this manner, and eat" - and since [the law] does not require showing it to a sage, this proves that he does not regard this as checking before the slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:6:2.hebrew: עד אחד נאמן באיסורין - דכל יחיד ויחיד האמינתו תורה, "וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך... ושחט את בן הבקר" (ויקרא א), ואכלי כהנים על ידו, ולא הזקיקו להעמיד עדים בדבר, ולא הצריכה תורה עדים אלא לעונש ממון או מיתת בית דין, ולעריות דגמרינן (גיטין צ.) "דבר" "דבר" מממון:
Rashi on Chullin 10b:6:2.english: One witness is believed with respect to prohibitions - For the Torah trusted each and every individual, [as it says,] "and you shall slaughter of your herd and of your flock... and he shall slaughter the young of the herd" (Leviticus 1), and the priests eat on his word [alone] - they were not required to bring witnesses in the matter. And the Torah required witnesses only for a monetary penalty or a death penalty imposed by the court; and for cases of forbidden relations, which we derive (Gittin 90a) by the verbal analogy of "davar"-"davar" from monetary law [that two witnesses are required].

Rashi on Chullin 10b:6:3.english: But did Rabbi Yoḥanan not say - This is [part of] the answer.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:7:1.english: That which the Sages said, etc. - In many places [the Sages] relied upon the presumption of status quo to forbid and to permit, like that [case] above.

Rashi on Chullin 10b:8:1.english: And the priest shall go out, etc. - For we require that he leave the entire house, and only afterward close the door. And although one could say that perhaps by the time he goes out and comes [back to close the door], its size will have diminished from a bean's-bulk, so that it turns out there was no nega at the time of the sealing, and his sealing would not be a valid sealing, since it is considered as if it [the nega] does not exist.

Tosafot on Chullin 10b:11:1.hebrew: כהן גדול ביום הכפורים יוכיח - תימה, דבפרק ידיעות הטומאה (שבועות יז:) אמרינן: הנכנס לבית המנוגע דרך אחוריו, אפילו כולו מבפנים חוץ מחוטמו, טהור; והבא אל הבית אמר רחמנא, דרך ביאה אסרה תורה. ויש לחלק בין כניסה ליציאה, דאורחא דמילתא ביציאה כתלמיד הנפטר מרבו:
Tosafot on Chullin 10b:11:1.english: The High Priest on Yom Kippur shall prove [it] - This is difficult: for in the chapter "Yedi'ot HaTum'ah" (Shevuot 17b) we say: one who enters a leprous house backward - even if his entire body is inside except for his nose - is pure; and [as for the phrase] "and he who comes into the house" (u-va el ha-bayit), the Torah forbade [only entry in] the normal manner of coming. And one can distinguish between entering and exiting, for the normal manner, when leaving, is like a student taking leave of his teacher [i.e., backward].

Tosafot on Chullin 10b:8:1.english: "And perhaps by the time it comes back out, the requisite measure is lacking, etc." - One should not ask, how is this proven from here, that we establish the matter according to its [prior] presumptive status (chazakah)? Perhaps here it is [deemed] impure only out of doubt, for a doubt of impurity in a private domain, its doubt is [deemed] impure, since in every case Scripture rendered it impure - even were it a public domain in which there are many people, and even [in the case of] a thing that has no da'at to be asked. But it is difficult, for that works out well where there is no [cause for] suspicion; but where there is a [cause for] suspicion, such as a knife that was found notched, and likewise [the case of] one of two [people], one of whom became definitely impure in a public domain, where we render both of them pure by reason of chazakah - in such a case, from where do we [derive] that we follow the chazakah? And one can answer that here too there is a great [cause for] suspicion, for even though it was found lacking after seven days, nevertheless they do not retroactively render pure all those who entered the house during the days of quarantine. However, this is difficult, for this matter is similar to a mikveh that was measured and found lacking, where we abandon the chazakah of the mikveh [that it was full] and render impure the man who immersed [in it], on account of [the principle] "establish the impure person on his [prior] presumptive status," and behold, the deficiency is right there before you. And so too here we should say that we abandon the chazakah of the nega and follow the person, whom we establish in a presumptive status of purity - and behold, the deficiency is right there before you.

Tosafot on Chullin 10b:8:2.hebrew: אלא לאו משום דאמרינן אוקמיה אחזקיה - ואין לומר דשאני הכא דאזלינן לחומרא, דמדאורייתא אין לחלק; ועוד דאף לקולא מטמאין ליה לשרוף קדשים ולהביא קרבן אם נכנס למקדש, וקא מייתי מספק חולין לעזרה; ועוד דאף לקולא מוקמינן הכא אחזקיה, דאי היה נגע גדול ובסוף השבוע היה חסר ממה שהיה, מטהרין; וניחוש דלמא אדנפיק ואתי בציר ליה שיעורא והיה כשיעור שהיה בסוף שבוע, ונמצא שהנגע עומד בעיניו ובעי הסגר שני; אלא משום דמוקמינן ליה בשעת הסגר אחזקיה:
Tosafot on Chullin 10b:8:2.english: Rather, is it not because we say: we establish it according to its presumptive status? - And one cannot say that here is different, in that we follow the stringent view, for according to Torah law there is no basis to distinguish [between a stringent and a lenient outcome]. And furthermore, even for a leniency, they render it impure, [requiring one] to burn sacred items and to bring an offering if he entered the Sanctuary, and he brings, on account of the doubt, non-sacred items into the Temple courtyard. And furthermore, even for a leniency, we establish [the mark] here according to its presumptive status: for if the mark had been large, and by the end of the week it was smaller than it had been, they would declare it pure. And should we be concerned lest, as he went out and came, the requisite measure diminished [further], so that it was [actually still] the same size as it had been at the end of the week, and it turns out that the mark stands exactly as it was and requires a second quarantine? Rather, [this is not a concern,] because we establish it, at the time of quarantine, according to its presumptive status.
